items.title: Reducing Batch Makespan for LLM Agent Workloads through Inference-Environment Coordination
items.summary_1line: Efficient batch execution of agent tasks is critical to LLM training and development workflows, including benchmark evaluation, synthetic-data generation, and RL rollouts. Since these tasks alternate between LLM infer...

editorial.tldr: This thread is a topical grouping of 27 arXiv preprints since Oct 26, not one event: what they share is reinforcement learning as a post-training method for LLMs and agents. Most of them work on one of three problems: what the reward should measure, how to train multi-turn tool-using agents, and how to pay for the rollouts.
editorial.whats_new: A Nov 12 preprint targets batch makespan for agent workloads, RL rollouts included, by coordinating LLM inference with environment execution, the third rollout-scheduling paper in this thread since Oct 27.
editorial.why_it_matters: For teams that post-train their own agents, the recurring constraints in these papers are rollout cost and reward design, and three of the 27 treat rollout scheduling as an infrastructure problem in its own right.
editorial.take_for_builders: Before adding GPUs to an agent RL or batch-eval pipeline, measure how much rollout wall-clock goes to environment execution and padding rather than inference, since that is the waste the three scheduling papers target.

beats.headline: Outcome-only rewards draw six papers on calibration, credit and guidance
beats.summary: These papers change what the policy is rewarded for: abstaining, matching confidence to correctness, or using the textual feedback a single outcome score discards.

beats.headline: RL moves onto the agent stack: harnesses, skills, memory and sub-agents
beats.summary: Ten papers apply RL to parts of an agent system rather than to a single-turn model, and one asks what multi-turn RL actually improves.

beats.headline: Three papers treat rollout scheduling as the bottleneck
beats.summary: Environment-aware scheduling on Oct 27, an offline scheduler for asynchronous LLM RL on Nov 6, and inference-environment coordination on Nov 12.

beats.headline: Eight clustered papers sit outside LLM agent post-training
beats.summary: Diffusion and flow fine-tuning, classical RL interpretability and theory, and two agent papers on voice benchmarks and shared-memory coordination.

open_questions: Do any of the three rollout-scheduling approaches ship as open-source code or get adopted in a public training stack?
Does an independent group reproduce the finding that multi-turn RL gains depend on sampling breadth and interaction depth?
Do the confidence-calibration methods for RLVR hold on agent tasks, beyond the RAG and reasoning settings they were proposed for?
Does co-evolving the harness with the policy beat tuning a harness for a fixed policy on a shared public benchmark?
